title: The album's track is looked up in the fixture's take list on the real side too
instrument: a parts-finish case composing album-video on the kernel with a takeId absent from KEPT_TAKES, asserting the words/render view's track.title is the take's title (not its id) and durationS is not null
body:
## Summary
app/(studio)/projects/[id]/_part/fixtureAlbum.ts:39-45 trackOf resolves the project's take through app/(studio)/projects/_port/fixtureData.ts KEPT_TAKES; the real side runs the same module, so a real take shows its id as the track title.

## Description
trackOf (app/(studio)/projects/[id]/_part/fixtureAlbum.ts:39) reads KEPT_TAKES, the produce FIXTURE's seed list, and falls back to { title: <take id>, durationS: null }. WORDS_KIND/RENDER_KIND are shared by both sides (kinds.ts LATER; real.ts draws views through later(kind).view), so on the real side every album project whose take is not one of the fixture's shows 'take-...' as its track, and the words editor's dry stand-in writes that id into the YouTube title. kinds.ts:27 states the rule this breaks: a module 'never falls back to a fixture'. Fixed: the side supplies the track (the real side from the sound store / plan, the fixture from KEPT_TAKES) through Ctx, and trackOf reads Ctx. Needs app/(studio)/projects/[id]/_part/realScene.ts (part-port-real-and-contract) to put the track on Ctx.

## Flow
- compose album-video on the kernel from a real kept take
- open /projects/<id>/words
- track reads the take id, durationS null; write-words (dry) titles the video with the id
- fix: Ctx.track built per side; trackOf reads it

## Expected impact
The album editors name the real track on the real side. Could break: parts-finish's album case if it relies on the fixture lookup.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - a module never falls back to a fixture
Before: real album with a non-fixture take: track.title = take id (by code read: fixtureAlbum.ts:43-44)
After: track.title = the take's title (predicted)
Method: simulation - the fix site is realScene.ts in part-port-real-and-contract; no real-side album case exists to read the figure
Result: better
Gate: none

title: A trailer's frames view offers a plate render its producer cannot price
instrument: a parts-frames case on a kernel trailer project with a composed spine and no stored frames record: the view's render-plates act has needs [] and the real actReceipt for it is ok with units == shot count
body:
## Summary
The frames module derives a trailer's shot units (app/(studio)/projects/[id]/_part/fixtureFrames.ts:68-85 chainOf, trailer lane) and offers 'render N plates'; the real producer's unitsOf (lib/producers/frames.ts:135-139) derives only an adopted explainer chain, so on the real side the receipt refuses 'render plates needs picture units'.

## Description
acts() (app/(studio)/projects/[id]/_part/fixtureFrames.ts:236-244) counts unitsOf(ctx, r), which falls back to chainOf - a trailer's SHOTS from the composed cut. The producer that prices and runs the act reads lib/producers/frames.ts unitsOf: the stored frames record, else the adopted explainer candidate; a trailer has none, so framesPlan refuses. Until an edit stores the units, the real editor shows an enabled act whose receipt is a refusal. Distinct from the open card 'Trailer shot plates are all asked for the same generic emblem' (that one is the subject a shot plate is booked with). Fixed: one derivation of the units both read (the module's chainOf lane rule moved where lib/producers/frames.ts can call it).

## Flow
- compose a trailer, compose its spine in research, open frames
- the act bar reads 'render 30 plates', needs none
- confirm -> receipt refused: render plates needs picture units
- fix: the producer derives units by the module's lane rule

## Expected impact
A trailer's first plate render is priced and runs instead of refusing. Could break: producer-step-frames cases that assume explainer-only derivation.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - one derivation of a part's units on both halves of a verb
Before: trailer, no stored frames: view offers render-plates (needs []), producer refuses (code read)
After: receipt prices N shot plates (predicted)
Method: simulation - the fix site is lib/producers/frames.ts (another context); building a kernel trailer with a composed spine is M
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
app/(studio)/projects/[id]/_part/fixtureFrames.ts:72-81 trailer lane: unitsFromRender(trailerRender(cut, ...), RENDERS[0])
lib/producers/frames.ts:135-139 unitsOf: rec units, else adopted explainer chain, else null
packages/producers/src/frames/define.ts:58 refuse(v.units.length === 0 ? "render plates needs picture units" : ...)

title: Any article record reads as a run whose five steps are all done
instrument: a part-editor-writing case: an article record with sections and no engine (an import) renders no 'done' step chips; a dry landing still renders its five
body:
## Summary
app/(studio)/projects/[id]/_part/fixtureExplainer.ts:54 articleData sets steps to research/outline/draft/check/critique all 'done' whenever the record has a title - on both sides, for records no run wrote.

## Description
The article record (@gt/domain/steps ARTICLE) carries title, sections and an optional engine; it carries no run steps. articleData fabricates STEPS.map(state 'done', usd null) for any titled record, so on the real side an imported article's rail shows five emerald 'done' chips for a run that never happened (the header at app/(studio)/projects/[id]/_part/fixtureExplainer.ts:20-24 says nothing lands this record yet but an import). That is the fixture drawing a state the record cannot evidence. Fixed: steps only where the record says a run produced it (engine present; the dry stand-in's engine is mode dry), else none - and the rail's empty state then needs a shape that does not say 'no run yet' over an imported article (Article.tsx:42-43, part-editor-writing-research's file).

## Flow
- import an article into an explainer project
- open the article part
- rail: research done, outline done, draft done, check done, critique done
- fix: steps from the record's evidence only

## Expected impact
The article rail stops claiming a run for an import. Could break: parts-explainer-gate expectations of steps.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - the rail shows only steps a record evidences
Before: titled article record with no engine: 5 'done' steps (code read)
After: 0 steps, a distinct empty shape (predicted)
Method: simulation - the right empty shape is a screen decision in Article.tsx (another context) that wants a photograph
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
app/(studio)/projects/[id]/_part/fixtureExplainer.ts:45 const STEPS = ["research", "outline", "draft", "check", "critique"] as const;
app/(studio)/projects/[id]/_part/fixtureExplainer.ts:54 steps: a.title === null ? [] : STEPS.map((name) => ({ name, state: "done" as const, usd: null })),

title: The fixture side never shows a part with a job running
body:
## Summary
app/(studio)/projects/[id]/_part/fixture.ts viewOf sets running: [] on every view; the real side fills it from live jobs (realScene.ts runningOf), so the editors' running state has no fixture to be built or photographed against.

## Description
Every fixture act lands at confirm (confirmAct -> landAct), and viewOf answers running: [] (app/(studio)/projects/[id]/_part/fixture.ts, the base frame). The real side answers the jobs in flight for the part (realScene.ts:56-65), and a live act longer than ACT_WAIT_MS returns with the view's running set (real.ts). The direction under parity is the other way round here: the fixture cannot reach a state the real side shows. Giving the fixture an in-flight job (a seeded running entry, or a dry act that lands on a later read) is a new fixture capability, not a parity repair - a direction call.

## Flow
- open any part on GRAVITONE_PRODUCE_SIDE=fixture
- confirm any act
- the view never carries running; the running affordance is never drawn

## Expected impact
Whoever builds the running state builds it blind, or against the real store. Could break: nothing until built.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - every view state the real port reaches has a fixture
Before: fixture views with running non-empty: 0 (viewOf hard-codes [])
After: at least one seeded part with a running job (proposed)
Method: simulation - a new fixture capability; the shape of an in-flight fixture job is a choice, not a figure
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: direction
evidence:
app/(studio)/projects/[id]/_part/fixture.ts viewOf: running: [],
app/(studio)/projects/[id]/_part/realScene.ts:84 running: runningOf(r, s.part.id, s.kind),

title: Memoize the fixture's step records per view (kctxOf records() per tab verdict)
body:
## Summary
kctxOf(ctx).records() re-encodes every planned later kind per verdict call, and tabsOf calls a verdict per tab - a suspected O(parts^2) per loadPart.

## Description
Timed with a throwaway vitest probe over all 8 fixture projects (warm, 5 passes): 1.2-2.3 ms per loadPart. There is no cost worth a cache and its invalidation.

## Flow
- probe loadPart over every editor part of every fixture project

## Expected impact
None measurable.

## Evaluation
Claim: performance - a faster fixture view
Before: 1.2-2.3 ms/loadPart (8 projects, 2-6 editors each)
After: not built - nothing to win
Method: probe - timed loop, probe deleted
Result: not-better
Gate: none
evidence: Rainshell 1.9 ms, night market 1.5, Salt lines 1.4, Glass Harbor 2.3, Bitcoin 1.6, quiet tariff 1.3, provider routing 1.2, port strike 1.3
